papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptome analyses unveil that MYH11 links stemness to immunotherapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy is an essential treatment strategy for lung cancer, yet resistance to it is often unavoidable, resulting in treatment failure and poor prognosis. The cancer stem cell (CSC) theory offers a valuable perspective for understanding tumor metastasis and resistance to immunotherapy. However, there is a scarcity of multi-omics studies that identify tumor stemness subpopulations and their associated signaling pathways. In this study, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with spatial transcriptomics sequencing (ST-seq) to identify a myosin heavy chain 11 (MYH11)-high stemnes
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to identify a stemness-associated subpopulation in non-small cell lung cancer marked by high expression of MYH11. The authors propose that MYH11 links cancer stemness to immunotherapy resistance, offering a potential biomarker or target for overcoming treatment failure.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals PDIA6 as a tumor-intrinsic driver of mesenchymal plasticity and vascular microenvironment remodeling in glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by pronounced microenvironmental heterogeneity, severe hypoxia, and profound resistance to conventional and targeted therapies. While abnormal tumor angiogenesis and perivascular niches are recognized hallmarks of GBM, the tumor-intrinsic drivers that actively orchestrate malignant-endothelial crosstalk and structure protective vascular sanctuaries remain to be fully defined. To identify key tumor-intrinsic vascular orchestrators, this study focused on PDIA6 and investigated its functional role and clinical significance in GBM mesenchymal plasticity, maligna
papers.summary: Using spatial transcriptomics on glioblastoma, the authors identify PDIA6 as a tumor-intrinsic factor that promotes mesenchymal plasticity and remodels the vascular microenvironment, potentially creating protective perivascular niches. This links a specific gene to malignant-endothelial crosstalk and highlights PDIA6 as a candidate driver of therapy resistance in GBM.

papers.title: Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence contributes to tumor progression and shapes the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet its prognostic and biological significance in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify senescence-associated prognostic signals through pan-cancer screening and to develop an integrated risk stratification framework for BLCA that bridges molecular characterization with translational relevance.
papers.summary: This study builds a senescence-associated prognostic model for bladder urothelial carcinoma by screening senescence-related signals across cancers and integrating multi-omics and pathological data. The model stratifies patients by risk and links senescence signatures to tumor microenvironment features, aiming to connect molecular characterization with potential clinical translation.

papers.title: Mouse spatial transcriptomics implicates the thalamus and cortex in autism and schizophrenia.
papers.abstract: The past decade has seen tremendous progress in the identification of genes associated with complex neuropsychiatric disorders, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia. Expression patterns of these genes in single cell data strongly implicate excitatory and inhibitory neurons; however, there are limited data on the brain regions involved - a critical question for neurobiology. Spatial transcriptomics provide an opportunity to perform systematic multi-regional analyses to provide insights into this question.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics in mouse brain to map where autism and schizophrenia risk genes are expressed across multiple regions. The analysis implicates the thalamus and cortex as key regions, extending prior single-cell findings that highlighted excitatory and inhibitory neurons. The work provides a systematic multi-regional view of neuropsychiatric risk gene expression.

papers.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
papers.abstract: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. Here, we analyzed a pan-pediatric scRNA-seq atlas of 266 patient- and xenograft-derived samples across 22 pediatric soli
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors analyzed a pan-pediatric single-cell RNA-seq atlas of 266 samples across 22 pediatric solid tumor types and found that these tumors express mixed neurodevelopmental gene programs reflecting their arrested progenitor origins. This lineage mixing reveals tumor-selective pairs of surface antigens that could serve as dual-targeting therapeutic vulnerabilities, since normal tissues would not co-express both antigens.

papers.title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.
papers.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data used in epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often overlook hierarchical relationships among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-type hierarchy, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. Across multiple simulated and real
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: HOMED is a new computational framework for DNA methylation deconvolution that accounts for hierarchical relationships among related cell types. It combines single-cell RNA-seq guidance and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data to optimize CpG signatures, improving cell-type proportion estimation across tissues and datasets.

papers.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical n
papers.summary: This review categorizes 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency (differentiation potential) from single-cell RNA-seq data into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based approaches. The authors analyze these methods under a unified mathematical framework, highlighting their differing assumptions and providing guidance for method selection. The work serves as a practical reference for researchers inferring cellular dynamics from static transcriptomic snapshots.

papers.title: CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis.
papers.abstract: The updated CellMarker 3.0 resource (http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CellMarker) offers a comprehensive resource, integrating experimentally validated and robustly algorithm-predicted marker genes for diverse cell types across human and mouse tissues. In addition, web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data are described. CellMarker 3.0 was updated with more data and new features, including (i) appending 274 tissues, 1877 cell types, 64 040 markers, and 1 245 923 tissue-cell type-marker entries over the previous version. The current release con
papers.summary: CellMarker 3.0 is an updated database that combines manually curated, experimentally validated cell marker genes with computationally predicted markers for many cell types in human and mouse tissues. It adds substantial new content over the previous version and introduces interactive web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data.

papers.title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
papers.abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing plat
papers.summary: The authors developed droplet-based long-read single-cell methods, dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT, that combine a commercial microfluidic device with nanopore sequencing to profile chromatin accessibility and histone modifications in individual cells at high throughput. This addresses the scalability bottleneck of prior long-read single-cell epigenomic approaches, enabling multidimensional regulatory element profiling per cell.

papers.title: Overlapping yet distinct spatiomolecular profiles across mood disorders and biological sex in the human prefrontal cortex.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD) exhibit both overlapping and distinct clinical features, including sex differences in prevalence and symptomatology, but how these similarities and differences are reflected at the molecular and cellular level in the human brain remains poorly understood. Here, we applied spatial transcriptomics to the human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex from individuals with MDD, BD, and neurotypical controls to resolve molecular programs associated with diagnosis and biological sex. Our analysis revealed sex- and diagnosis-specific differences across
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used spatial transcriptomics on human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex to compare molecular profiles across major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, and neurotypical controls, focusing on both diagnosis and biological sex. The authors found overlapping yet distinct spatiomolecular signatures associated with each mood disorder and with sex, suggesting that shared and divergent clinical features have molecular correlates in the brain.

papers.title: Overcoming segmentation bottlenecks in brain tissue for spatial proteomic inference at population scale.
papers.abstract: In spatial proteomics across large cohorts, downstream estimates from tens of thousands of images depend on accurate cell segmentation. Yet pretrained segmentation models struggle with morphologically complex cell bodies in human brain tissue, and how domain adaptation affects downstream discovery remains unclear. Here, we introduce SPInfer, a workflow for spatial proteomic inference developed using 5,832 manually annotated cell bodies from 120 immunofluorescence images of the human prefrontal cortex. After benchmarking eight segmentation methods spanning classical, convolutional, and foundati
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present SPInfer, a workflow for spatial proteomic inference that addresses cell segmentation challenges in human brain tissue. Using 5,832 manually annotated cell bodies from 120 immunofluorescence images of the prefrontal cortex, they benchmark eight segmentation methods and show how domain adaptation affects downstream discovery at population scale.

papers.title: spaTransfer: transfer learning for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data using non-negative matrix factorization.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in spatially-resolved transcriptomics have enabled profiling of gene expression in a spatial context, which has led to the generation of large-scale single-cell and spatial atlases with computationally-derived cell type or spatial domain labels. An increasingly important task with these data has become the transfer of cell type or spatial domain annotations from a given reference (or source) atlas into a new target tissue or sample. The reference and target datasets could be at different resolutions or measured on different experimental platforms. Here, we present a method to p
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: spaTransfer is a new computational method that uses non-negative matrix factorization to transfer cell type or spatial domain labels from a reference single-cell or spatial transcriptomics atlas to a new target sample, even when the two datasets differ in resolution or were generated on different platforms. This addresses a key challenge in leveraging large annotated atlases for annotating new spatial data.

papers.title: Denoising single-cell ATAC-seq data with Shannon entropy.
papers.abstract: Single-cell Assay for Transposase Accessible Chromatin with sequencing (scATAC-seq) is widely used to investigate chromatin accessibility but experiments often contain empty droplets, droplets containing damaged nuclei or cellular-debris. Accurately filtering high-quality nuclei is important as noisy droplets contribute reads that can distort downstream analysis and obscure rare cell population. Current approaches often rely on read depth and or predefined genomic features that are not exactly the same as chromatin accessibility landscape. Here, we present a Shannon entropy-based method that f
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce a Shannon entropy-based method for filtering low-quality droplets (empty, damaged nuclei, or debris) from single-cell ATAC-seq data. Unlike existing approaches that rely on read depth or predefined genomic features, this method uses the information content of the chromatin accessibility signal itself to distinguish high-quality nuclei. This improves downstream analysis by removing noisy droplets that can distort results and obscure rare cell populations.

papers.title: CellWHISPER disentangles direct cell-cell communication from structural proximity.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics makes it possible to infer direct, contact-dependent cellular communication, but existing tools are prone to high error rates due to spatial structure in cell types and gene expression. We present CellWHISPER, a framework for inferring contact-mediated communication, including gap junctions and ligand-receptor signaling, from spatial transcriptomics data. CellWHISPER controls errors with a statistical procedure that accounts for confounding effects of cell-type-specific expression and spatial organization. Closed-form significance scores enable analysis of large data. A
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CellWHISPER is a new computational framework for inferring direct, contact-dependent cell-cell communication (gap junctions and ligand-receptor signaling) from spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses a key problem in existing tools—high error rates caused by confounding spatial structure in cell types and gene expression—using a statistical procedure with closed-form significance scores that scales to large datasets.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Quality Control Reshapes Spatially Resolved Metabolic Flux Predictions in Prostate Cancer.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables region-resolved investigation of tumor metabolism, yet translating gene expression into reliable metabolic flux predictions remains challenging because genome-scale models can admit thermodynamically infeasible cycles (TICs). Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomic data from twelve annotated regions of a single prostate tumor, spanning normal, inflamed, and Gleason 3+3 and 3+4 tissues, with Human-GEM using an E-Flux framework incorporating defined nutrient constraints, explicit cycle certification, and loopless flux variability analysis. An initial naïve impl
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors integrated spatial transcriptomics from twelve annotated regions of a single prostate tumor with a genome-scale metabolic model (Human-GEM) using an E-Flux framework, adding explicit thermodynamic cycle certification and loopless flux variability analysis. They show that genome-scale models can admit thermodynamically infeasible cycles (TICs) that distort spatially resolved metabolic flux predictions, and that applying thermodynamic quality control reshapes those predictions across normal, inflamed, and Gleason 3+3/3+4 tissue regions.

papers.title: X-SPEAR: An Extensible Framework for Spatial Panel Evaluation and Refinement.
papers.abstract: Targeted spatial transcriptomics platforms such as 10x Genomics Xenium measure a predefined panel of genes. A gene is usually detected in fewer cells in the spatial assay than in the single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) reference used to choose it, by an amount that differs from gene to gene. We present eXtensible Spatial Panel Evaluation And Refinement (X- SPEAR), a framework for designing and checking Xenium gene panels. Its marker-selection method, Decision-rule Aggregation for Rare-cell Typing (DART), learns short Boolean gene rules and keeps several gene-disjoint rules per cell type. DA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: X-SPEAR is a framework for designing and evaluating targeted spatial transcriptomics gene panels, addressing the problem that genes chosen from scRNA-seq references are often detected in fewer cells in spatial assays, with gene-specific dropout. Its marker-selection method, DART, learns short Boolean gene rules and retains multiple gene-disjoint rules per cell type to improve rare-cell typing. This provides a systematic approach to panel design and quality control for platforms like 10x Xenium.

papers.title: Survival-associated cellular communication networks in human solid cancers.
papers.abstract: Single-cell atlases have enabled the prediction of human cell-cell communication (CCC) networks in cancer, but whether predicted communication networks have clinical significance is not well understood. Here, we integrated a pan-solid cancer scRNA-seq atlas comprising 78 cell types from 318,426 quality-controlled cells with bulk RNA-seq and clinical outcome data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) to develop Single-cell-based Kaplan-Meier Analysis Network (SKyNet). SKyNet prioritizes ligand-receptor interactions associated with overall survival across 11 human solid cancers, predicting unique
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed SKyNet, a method that integrates single-cell RNA-seq cell-cell communication networks with bulk RNA-seq and clinical outcome data from TCGA to identify ligand-receptor interactions associated with overall survival across 11 solid cancers. By combining a pan-cancer atlas of 318,426 cells and 78 cell types with survival data, they prioritize communication networks that have clinical relevance, revealing cancer-specific survival-associated interactions.

papers.title: Dose-additive and dose-dependent fetal testis toxicity of a nine-phthalate mixture in the rat.
papers.abstract: Phthalates (ortho-phthalic acid diesters) are used in a variety of manufacturing processes, particularly as non-covalent plasticizers in flexible polyvinyl chloride. Phthalates are male reproductive toxicants that disrupt the development of the fetal testis, resulting in malformed seminiferous cords, multinucleated germ cells (MNGs), and decreased testosterone production. We previously reported that MNGs were a sensitive, dose-dependent marker of dipentyl phthalate (DPEP) germ cell toxicity. To test whether germ cell effects of phthalates are dose-additive, we measured the induction of MNGs by
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study tested whether the fetal testis toxicity of a nine-phthalate mixture in rats follows dose-additive principles, using multinucleated germ cells (MNGs) as a sensitive marker. The authors found that the mixture's effects were dose-additive and dose-dependent, supporting the assumption that phthalates with a common mechanism of action can be assessed jointly in risk assessment.

papers.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
papers.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. Existing supervised approaches rely on accurate reference data, which are lacking for many cancer types, whereas unsupervised
papers.summary: CDState is a computational method that deconvolves bulk tumor RNA sequencing data to resolve intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity into distinct malignant cell states without requiring reference data. This unsupervised approach offers a scalable alternative to single-cell RNA sequencing for studying cell-state diversity across large cancer cohorts.

papers.title: SVC: A Vision Transformer-based Spatially and Virtually Embedded Cell Model for Deciphering Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomic Heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Subcellular transcript localization shapes gene regulation and cellular function, yet profiling it at scale remains difficult, limiting our ability to study subcellular heterogeneity across tissues and disease. Here, we present SVC, a Vision Transformer-based spatially and virtually embedded cell model that learns subcellular transcript organization within native tissue context directly from subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics. SVC represents each gene's subcellular localization as an image patch and uses other genes within the same cell as context, enabling subcellular contextual l
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SVC is a Vision Transformer-based model that learns subcellular transcript organization directly from subcellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics data. It represents each gene's subcellular localization as an image patch and uses other genes in the same cell as context, enabling contextual analysis of subcellular spatial heterogeneity across tissues and disease.

papers.title: CQRM: A Composite Quantile Regression Model for Differential Expression Analysis of Non-Coding RNA Count Data.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) play important roles in various biological processes, primarily via regulating gene expression at multiple levels. Nevertheless, compared to protein-coding genes, ncRNAs are relatively understudied. They are characterized by low expression, large variation, and more dynamic expression across different tissues and cell types, which creates unique challenges in differential expression (DE) analysis. Methods: We propose the CQRM, an adaptive multi-quantile testing framework for ncRNA count data that incorporates jittering to accommodate discrete cou
papers.summary: The authors propose CQRM, a composite quantile regression framework for differential expression analysis of non-coding RNA count data. It uses adaptive multi-quantile testing with jittering to handle the discrete, low-expression, and highly variable nature of ncRNA counts, addressing limitations of standard DE methods for this data type.

papers.title: ALBIS: simulation of multi-resolution and multi-dimensional spatial transcriptomics data.
papers.abstract: The rapid adoption of spatial transcriptomics (ST) technologies has been accompanied by substantial growth in computational methods, creating an increasing need for systematic and reliable benchmarking, particularly as analyses increasingly extend from individual tissue sections to three-dimensional (3D) tissue reconstruction. Existing benchmarks often rely on a small and similar set of experimentally-derived datasets because they offer a reliable ground truth label, which is hard to find in practice. Simulated or synthetic data provide an alternative, yet most existing simulators either adapt
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: ALBIS is a new simulator for spatial transcriptomics data that generates synthetic datasets at multiple resolutions and dimensions, including 3D tissue reconstruction. It addresses the benchmarking gap caused by reliance on a small set of experimental datasets with limited ground truth, offering a flexible alternative for systematically evaluating computational methods.

papers.title: Deep-learning-driven tumor microenvironment profiling improves immunotherapy response prediction.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed the management of many cancers, such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), yet durable clinical benefit is achieved in only a subset of patients. Immunotherapy outcomes are governed by the multicellular tumor microenvironment (TME), through the structured and directional interplay of regulatory programs and ligand-receptor communications. Yet most existing methods for immunotherapy response prediction rely on independent signatures or cell types and fail to model the structured and directional signaling network within the TME. To address this gap, we introdu
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present a deep-learning framework that profiles the tumor microenvironment by modeling structured, directional ligand-receptor signaling networks rather than relying on independent gene signatures or cell types. Applied to clear cell renal cell carcinoma, this network-aware approach improves prediction of immunotherapy response compared with existing methods. The work suggests that capturing multicellular communication structure, not just cell-type abundance, is key to forecasting clinical benefit.

papers.title: Spatially resolved tumor-microenvironment architecture defines therapeutic response in unresectable hepatoblastoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatoblastoma exhibits variable therapeutic response that is not fully explained by current risk stratification. While prior studies have characterized tumor composition, the role of spatial organization in determining outcome, particularly in unresectable disease requiring transplantation under immunosuppression, remains unclear.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint uses spatially resolved profiling to map the tumor microenvironment architecture in unresectable hepatoblastoma, a pediatric liver cancer. The authors find that the spatial organization of tumor and immune cells, beyond bulk tumor composition, is associated with how patients respond to therapy, including in transplant recipients on immunosuppression. This suggests spatial features could improve risk stratification for this disease.

papers.title: An integrated multi-omic atlas of the choroid plexus highlights conserved molecular programs of epithelial function.
papers.abstract: The choroid plexus (ChP) is a specialized epithelial tissue responsible for production of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), maintenance of the blood-CSF barrier and regulation of CSF-borne signaling factors. However, despite the ChP's central role in CSF homeostasis, conserved molecular programs of ChP epithelial function across species and conditions remain incompletely defined. In this study, we integrated eight mouse and human single-cell/nucleus RNA-seq datasets to build a multi-species ChP atlas capturing major epithelial, stromal, vascular, and immune populations. Cross-dataset differential exp
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study integrates eight mouse and human single-cell/nucleus RNA-seq datasets to build a multi-species atlas of the choroid plexus, a brain tissue that produces cerebrospinal fluid and maintains the blood-CSF barrier. By comparing cell populations across datasets and species, the authors identify conserved molecular programs underlying epithelial function, providing a reference for understanding choroid plexus biology and CSF homeostasis.

papers.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
papers.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug se
papers.summary: The authors present CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that first deconvolves bulk RNA-seq data into cell-type composition and cell-type-specific expression, then uses that information to infer drug sensitivity from bulk transcriptomes. This enables drug-response analyses that account for cellular heterogeneity rather than treating bulk samples as homogeneous.

papers.title: Detection of Supporting-Cell-Associated Gene Transcripts in Adult Human Cochlear Tissue from Cadaveric Temporal Bones.
papers.abstract: The adult human cochlea is difficult to study because viable inner-ear tissue is rarely available and postmortem samples are technically challenging to process. Supporting cells are essential for cochlear architecture, ionic and osmotic balance, synaptic stability, stress responses, and potential regenerative signaling. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the feasibility of detecting transcripts associated with cochlear supporting-cell biology in adult human cadaveric cochlear tissue.
papers.summary: This study tested whether gene transcripts related to cochlear supporting cells could be detected in adult human inner-ear tissue collected postmortem from cadaveric temporal bones. The authors demonstrate that such transcripts are detectable, suggesting that cadaveric cochlear tissue is a feasible source for molecular studies of supporting-cell biology despite the technical challenges of processing postmortem inner-ear samples.

papers.title: PathwayFinder enables linked exploration of cell types and gene modules in spatially resolved transcriptomics data.
papers.abstract: The rapid development of spatially resolved transcriptomics technologies has provided opportunities and challenges for understanding biological systems. Interpreting these data requires integrated analysis of gene expression and cell types within their spatial context, however, existing tools fall short in scaling this linked interactive exploration to large-scale datasets. We present PathwayFinder, a visual analytics application designed to bridge the gap between gene-centric and cell-centric analysis. Unlike standard workflows that view cells and genes in isolation, PathwayFinder links them
papers.summary: PathwayFinder is a visual analytics tool for spatially resolved transcriptomics data that links gene-centric and cell-centric analyses, allowing users to interactively explore gene modules and cell types together in their spatial context. It addresses the scalability limitations of existing tools for large datasets, enabling integrated exploration rather than viewing cells and genes in isolation.

papers.title: The CD39/CD73 adenosinergic pathway is increased by proinflammatory states and modified by chemo-radiation in human non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Recent clinical trials show prominent anti-tumor activity of CD73-blocking antibodies in combination with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) antagonists in a subset of patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which highlights the need to understand the properties of the CD39/CD73 pathway in human lung malignancies and its modulation by other anti-cancer therapies. To address this, we study the distribution, biological context, spatial heterogeneity, clinical significance, and modulation of CD39/CD73 using multiplexed quantitative immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomic
papers.summary: This study maps the CD39/CD73 adenosinergic pathway in human non-small cell lung cancer using multiplexed immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomics, showing that proinflammatory states increase pathway expression and that chemo-radiation modifies it. The findings help explain how this immunosuppressive pathway varies across tumors and is shaped by standard therapies, informing combination strategies with CD73-blocking antibodies.

papers.title: Dupilumab modulates type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor-expressing immune cells in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis.
papers.abstract: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (eCRS) is a refractory type 2 inflammatory disease characterized by nasal polyp formation and eosinophilic infiltration. Although dupilumab, an IL-4Rα-blocking antibody, demonstrates clinical efficacy, its cellular mechanisms within nasal polyps remain unclear.
papers.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
papers.summary: This study investigates how dupilumab, an antibody blocking the IL-4 receptor alpha chain, affects immune cells in nasal polyps of patients with eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis. The authors characterize changes in type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor-expressing immune cell populations, providing cellular-level insight into the drug's mechanism of action in this refractory type 2 inflammatory disease.

papers.title: BGN marks cancer-associated fibroblast activation and extracellular matrix remodeling in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: Biglycan (BGN) is an important component of the extracellular matrix (ECM). Using an integrated analysis of TCGA bulk RNA-sequencing, single-cell RNA-sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic datasets, we systematically characterized the expression patterns, prognostic significance, and biological roles of BGN in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and survival analyses in independent clinical cohorts further validated the expression pattern, abundance, and prognostic significance of BGN. The biological role of BGN was further investigated using
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data to show that biglycan (BGN) marks activated cancer-associated fibroblasts and extracellular matrix remodeling in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. BGN expression is validated by western blotting and immunohistochemistry in independent cohorts and is associated with prognosis, suggesting it as a marker of fibroblast activation and a potential prognostic biomarker in HNSCC.

papers.title: Novel adenoma-immune phenotypes are associated with risk of metachronous polyps and colorectal cancer in a bowel screening cohort.
papers.abstract: Current British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines misclassify metachronous lesion risk after polypectomy in approximately 40% of patients. Building on evidence that immune exclusion drives progression of adenomas to colorectal cancer, this study examined immune profiles in screen-detected adenomas as a predictive biomarker for metachronous lesion risk.
papers.summary: This study examined immune cell profiles in screen-detected colorectal adenomas to predict the risk of developing new polyps or colorectal cancer later (metachronous lesions). The authors identify novel adenoma-immune phenotypes that are associated with metachronous lesion risk, suggesting immune profiling could improve on current BSG guidelines, which misclassify risk in about 40% of patients.

papers.title: Response to comments on "SpatialDG: a novel spatial domain identification method for spatially resolved transcriptomics data based on dual-graph neural network".
papers.abstract: We respond to concerns regarding reference-label-informed epoch selection in SpatialDG. We acknowledge this limitation and report a matched DLPFC reevaluation of SpatialDG and Spatial-MGCN under the same reference-label-independent checkpoint-selection rule, in which SpatialDG achieved the higher three-seed mean ARI on all 12 slices.
papers.summary: This is an author response addressing criticisms of SpatialDG, a dual-graph neural network method for identifying spatial domains in spatially resolved transcriptomics data. The main concern was that SpatialDG used reference labels to select model epochs, potentially inflating performance. In a re-evaluation on DLPFC data using a reference-label-independent checkpoint-selection rule applied equally to SpatialDG and Spatial-MGCN, SpatialDG still achieved higher three-seed mean ARI across all 12 slices.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted meta-classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe) so that method weighting varies by edge rather than being fixed globally. They also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, the approach aims to resolve disagreements between methods more effectively than picking one method or simple averaging.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data from NSCLC patients to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) based on epithelial cell-derived genes, using machine learning to stratify patients by survival and immune activity. Low-PIS patients show better outcomes and higher immune infiltration, and ADAM12 is validated as a key functional regulator through cell line and mouse experiments. The work links epithelial cell states to immunotherapy response prediction in lung cancer.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent computational methods for inferring cell-cell communication from spatial transcriptomics data into three groups: cell-type or single-cell resolution network inference, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability, and regulatory modulation. It highlights how spatial context enables more biologically grounded communication inference than scRNA-seq alone and maps methods to the distinct biological questions they address.

papers.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: The authors introduce a Contextual Activity Score (CAS) that infers ADAR-associated RNA editing activity directly from gene expression data, bypassing the need for raw sequencing reads required by the standard Alu Editing Index. This enables ADAR activity estimation across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics platforms where the AEI is impractical.

papers.title: An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of alternative polyadenylation (APA) in neuroblastoma, a common pediatric solid tumor. The authors identify NUDT21 as a key regulator that coordinates transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuits to sustain neuroblastoma cell proliferation and survival, suggesting that APA machinery may be a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Contrasting Spatial Genomic Structure in Two Widespread Grassland Species Across Norway Supports Species-Specific Seed Sourcing.
papers.abstract: Ecological restoration typically relies on locally sourced seed material, yet seed sourcing in many countries is based on broad administrative regions rather than empirical genetic data. Whether these generalized zones reflect biologically meaningful population genomic structure, particularly among co-occurring species used together in restoration, remains poorly understood, thus limiting genetically informed restoration practices. Here, we use genome-wide double-digest RAD sequencing (ddRAD-seq) to examine spatial population genomic structure in two widespread perennial grassland species comm
papers.summary: Using ddRAD-seq, the authors compared spatial population genomic structure in two widespread perennial grassland species across Norway and found that the species differ in how their genetic variation is partitioned geographically. This means that broad administrative seed-sourcing zones do not capture biologically meaningful population structure equally well for co-occurring restoration species, supporting species-specific seed sourcing guidelines.

papers.title: An ibuprofen-eluting electrospun membrane prevents ureteral fibrosis by dampening macrophage-associated fibroblast activation.
papers.abstract: Ureteral stricture is driven by unresolved inflammation and progressive matrix deposition, yet mechanism-guided local therapies remain limited.
papers.summary: This study develops an electrospun membrane that locally releases ibuprofen to prevent ureteral stricture (scarring) after injury. The authors show that the anti-inflammatory drug dampens macrophage-driven activation of fibroblasts, reducing fibrosis in a preclinical model. The work suggests a mechanism-guided local therapy for a condition with few effective treatments.

papers.title: Decoding pyroptosis at single-cell resolution: heterogeneity, microenvironment remodeling and potential translational insights.
papers.abstract: Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory programmed cell death mediated by inflammatory caspases and Gasdermin (GSDM) family proteins, exerts dual roles in host defense and pathological damage. Traditional bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) is limited in capturing single-cell heterogeneity and dissecting intercellular communication, impeding in-depth mechanistic exploration of pyroptosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these limitations, enabling high-throughput profiling of single-cell transcriptomes and precise characterization of gene expression heter
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell RNA sequencing can be used to study pyroptosis, an inflammatory form of programmed cell death, at the level of individual cells. It highlights how scRNA-seq overcomes the limitations of bulk sequencing in capturing cellular heterogeneity and intercellular communication, and explores implications for microenvironment remodeling and translational applications.

papers.title: Reanalysis of public bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomes identifies widespread tumor-normal dysregulation and a cross-layer cell-cycle signal in sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCC) is a rare malignancy affecting the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection identified as a critical etiological factor in a subset of cases. HPV-positive and HPV-negative SNSCC exhibit distinct clinical behaviors, with HPV-positive tumors generally demonstrating better prognosis and treatment response. However, the cellular composition and transcriptomic landscape of SNSCC tumor versus normal tissue remain incompletely characterized. Multi-layer transcriptomic reanalysis of publicly available single-nucleus and bul
papers.summary: The authors reanalyzed public bulk and single-nucleus transcriptome datasets to compare tumor and normal tissue in sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma, a rare head and neck cancer. They report widespread tumor-normal gene expression dysregulation and identify a cell-cycle signal that appears consistently across both bulk and single-nucleus data layers. The work also highlights differences between HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumors, though the findings are based entirely on reanalysis of existing public data.

papers.title: Topology-adjusted knockout (TAKO): interpretable in silico single-gene knockout ranking on wild-type single-cell gene regulatory networks.
papers.abstract: Predicting single-gene knockout effects from wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data remains challenging when perturbation experiments are costly and existing approaches require knockout-specific model training. Here we introduce Topology-Adjusted Knockout (TAKO), a computationally efficient WT-only framework for single-gene KO impact ranking on single-cell gene regulatory networks. The method applies a strict cut-in-and-out intervention on network transition dynamics and quantifies impact by contrasting stationary propagation profiles before and after perturbation under the same restart distributi
papers.summary: TAKO is a new computational framework that predicts the effects of knocking out individual genes using only wild-type single-cell RNA-seq data, without needing any knockout experiments for training. It works by building a gene regulatory network from the data and simulating gene removal through a 'cut-in-and-out' intervention on network dynamics, then ranking genes by how much their removal changes the network's steady-state behavior. This makes knockout impact prediction cheaper and more interpretable for single-cell studies.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis identifies monocyte/macrophage senescence-associated candidate genes in pulmonary arterial hypertension.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by immune dysregulation and vascular remodeling. Cellular senescence modulates immune responses, but its role in PAH, particularly in monocytes/macrophages, remains unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify senescence-associated candidate genes associated with monocytes/macrophages in PAH.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic datasets to identify senescence-associated genes specifically in monocytes/macrophages in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The authors propose candidate genes linking immune cell senescence to PAH vascular remodeling, though the findings are computational and require experimental validation.

papers.title: Investigating the Expression and Function of PPP2R1A in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multi-Omics Analysis with in vitro Validation.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains difficult to diagnose early and to treat effectively. Protein Phosphatase 2A Regulatory Subunit Aα (PPP2R1A), the scaffolding (Aα) subunit of the PP2A holoenzyme, is altered in several cancer types, but its expression pattern, functional significance, and translational relevance in HCC are incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates the expression and functional role of PPP2R1A, a scaffolding subunit of the PP2A phosphatase complex, in hepatocellular carcinoma using multi-omics data combined with in vitro experiments. The authors characterize how PPP2R1A expression is altered in HCC and assess its potential functional and translational relevance, though the abstract does not yet report specific findings.

papers.title: Immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor axes in osteoarthritis: microenvironmental control of inflammation, matrix remodeling, and chondrocyte fate.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is increasingly recognized as a whole-joint disease shaped by chronic low-grade inflammation, matrix damage, mechanical stress, and failed tissue repair. Beyond the traditional view of cartilage wear, emerging evidence indicates that immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor (LR) communication plays a central role in translating microenvironmental cues into disease-relevant chondrocyte phenotypes. In this narrative review, we summarize major immune-derived or inflammation-amplified LR axes that regulate OA progression, including cytokine pathways such as IL-1β-IL-1R, TNF-α-TNFR, I
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that osteoarthritis is a whole-joint disease driven by chronic low-grade inflammation, in which ligand-receptor communication between immune cells and chondrocytes translates microenvironmental cues into disease-relevant chondrocyte phenotypes. It catalogs major immune-derived or inflammation-amplified axes (e.g., IL-1β–IL-1R, TNF-α–TNFR) that regulate inflammation, matrix remodeling, and chondrocyte fate. The review frames these immune-chondrocyte interactions as central to OA progression rather than cartilage wear alone.

papers.title: A curvilinear coordinate flatmap for visualizing hippocampal structure and development.
papers.abstract: The hippocampal formation is a highly curved and topographically complex forebrain structure. This complex geometry presents persistent challenges for analyzing subregional, laminar, and connectivity patterns. Here, we present a computational workflow that generates curvilinear-coordinate flatmaps from mouse Common Coordinate Framework (CCF) registered hippocampal and retrohippocampal regions by solving the Laplacian equation to derive geodesic streamlines. This transformation unfolds the hippocampus into a planar slab, bounded by the meningeal and ventricular surfaces, with the depth defined
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational workflow that unfolds the curved, topographically complex hippocampal formation into a flat, planar map using curvilinear coordinates derived from solving the Laplacian equation. This flatmap preserves geodesic relationships and defines depth between meningeal and ventricular surfaces, enabling clearer visualization and analysis of subregional, laminar, and connectivity patterns in mouse hippocampal data registered to the Common Coordinate Framework.

papers.title: A Spatial Multiomics Atlas and Resource for Immune-Fibrotic Niches in Chronic Kidney Allograft Dysfunction.
papers.abstract: Chronic allograft dysfunction (CAD) is a major cause of late kidney-allograft failure, yet its spatially organized cellular and metabolic mechanisms remain poorly resolved because human biopsies are scarce and experimental models are imperfect. Here, we established a tacrolimus-modulated accelerated mouse model of CAD and constructed a cross-species multiomics atlas by integrating mouse single-cell RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and multiplex imaging with human single-nucleus RNA sequencing, Visium HD spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics. Cross-species analysis revealed conserved
papers.summary: This study builds a cross-species spatial multiomics atlas of chronic kidney allograft dysfunction by combining a tacrolimus-modulated accelerated mouse model with human biopsy data, integrating single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq, flow cytometry, multiplex imaging, Visium HD spatial transcriptomics, and spatial metabolomics. The atlas identifies conserved immune-fibrotic niches and their spatially organized cellular and metabolic features, providing a resource for understanding late allograft failure.
